1: Once again, mighty-armed one, hear my supreme word. You are delighted, and I will speak it to you out of a wish for your good.
2: Neither the hosts of gods nor the great seers know my origin. For in every way I am the beginning of the gods and of the great seers.
3: Whoever knows me as unborn and without beginning, the great lord of the worlds, is undeluded among mortals and is freed from all evils.
4: There is buddhi, knowledge, freedom from delusion, forbearance, truth, self-restraint and calm. There is pleasure and pain, coming to be and ceasing to be, fear and fearlessness too.
5: There is non-harm, evenness, contentment, austerity, giving, fame and ill fame. These states of beings, in their different kinds, arise from me alone.
6: The seven great seers, the four ancient ones and likewise the Manus had my nature and were born of the mind. From them come these creatures in the world.
7: Whoever truly knows this manifestation and yoga of mine is joined by unshaking yoga. Of this there is no doubt.
8: I am the origin of all, and from me all proceeds. Thinking this, the wise worship me, filled with feeling.
9: With their thoughts on me and their life-breath gone to me, they awaken one another and are always telling of me, and they are content and they delight.
10: To them, constantly joined and worshipping with love, I give that buddhi-yoga by which they come to me.
11: Out of compassion for them alone, I, abiding in the state of the self, destroy the darkness born of ignorance with the shining lamp of knowledge.
12: You are the supreme brahman, the supreme abode, the supreme purifier. You are the eternal divine person, the first god, unborn and all-pervading.
13: That is what all the seers call you, and likewise the divine seer Nārada, Asita, Devala and Vyāsa. And indeed you yourself tell me so.
14: I think all this that you say to me is true, Keśava. For neither the gods nor the Dānavas know your manifestation, blessed lord.
15: You alone know yourself, through your own self, highest of persons, bringer forth of beings, lord of beings, god of gods, master of the world.
16: You ought to tell me of them, leaving nothing out, for your own manifestations are divine: the manifestations by which you stand pervading these worlds.
17: How may I know you, yogī, as I think of you always? And in which of the many states am I to think of you, blessed lord?
18: Tell me again, at length, of your own yoga and manifestation, Janārdana. For I never have my fill of hearing this nectar.
19: Come, I will tell you the chief of them, best of the Kurus, for my own manifestations are divine. There is no end to my extent.
20: I am the self, Guḍākeśa, seated in the heart of all beings. I am the beginning, the middle and indeed the end of beings.
21: Of the Ādityas I am Viṣṇu. Of lights I am the radiant sun. Of the Maruts I am Marīci. Of the lunar mansions I am the moon.
22: Of the Vedas I am the Sāma Veda. Of the gods I am Vāsava. And of the senses I am the mind. Of beings I am consciousness.
23: And of the Rudras I am Śaṅkara. Of the yakṣas and rākṣasas I am the lord of wealth. And of the Vasus I am fire. Of peaked mountains I am Meru.
24: And know me, son of Pṛthā, as Bṛhaspati, the chief of household priests. Of army commanders I am Skanda. Of bodies of water I am the ocean.
25: Of the great seers I am Bhṛgu. Of utterances I am the one syllable. Of sacrifices I am the sacrifice of murmured recitation. Of immovable things I am the Himālaya.
26: Of all trees I am the sacred fig tree, and of the divine seers I am Nārada. Of the gandharvas I am Citraratha. Of the perfected ones I am the sage Kapila.
27: Of horses know me as Uccaiḥśravas, born of the nectar of immortality. Of lordly elephants know me as Airāvata, and of men as the ruler of men.
28: Of weapons I am the thunderbolt. Of cows I am the cow that yields whatever is desired. And I am Kandarpa, the begetter. Of serpents I am Vāsuki.
29: And of the nāgas I am Ananta. Of water creatures I am Varuṇa. And of the ancestors I am Aryaman. Of those who restrain I am Yama.
30: And of the daityas I am Prahlāda. Of those who reckon I am time. And of wild animals I am the lord of animals, and of birds I am the son of Vinatā.
31: Of purifiers I am the wind. Of those who bear weapons I am Rāma. And of fish I am the makara. Of streams I am the daughter of Jahnu.
32: Of creations I am the beginning and the end, and the middle too, Arjuna. Of kinds of knowledge I am the knowledge of the self. Of those who debate I am the argument.
33: Of letters I am the letter a, and of the compounds I am the pair compound. I alone am undecaying time. I am the ordainer, who faces in every direction.
34: And I am death, which carries off all, and I am the origin of things that are yet to be. Of feminine things I am fame, fortune and speech, memory, intelligence, steadfastness and forbearance.
35: Likewise, of chants I am the Bṛhat chant. Of metres I am the Gāyatrī. Of months I am Mārgaśīrṣa. Of seasons I am the one that is a mine of flowers.
36: Of those who cheat I am gambling. I am the splendour of the splendid. I am victory. I am resolve. I am the sattva of those who have sattva.
37: Of the Vṛṣṇis I am the son of Vasudeva. Of the sons of Pāṇḍu I am the winner of wealth. Of sages, too, I am Vyāsa, and of poets I am the poet Uśanas.
38: I am the rod of those who subdue. I am the right conduct of those who wish to conquer. And I am the silence of secret things. I am the knowledge of those who have knowledge.
39: And whatever is the seed of all beings, that too I am, Arjuna. There is no being, moving or unmoving, that could exist without me.
40: There is no end to my divine manifestations of power, scorcher of foes. But what I have told you of the extent of that manifested power is given by way of example.
41: Whatever being has power, has fortune or is indeed mighty, understand that every such one has arisen from a portion of my splendour.
42: Or rather, Arjuna, what use is it to you to know all this? I stand, holding up this whole world with a single portion.
